key_insight: System-level defenses—combining dynamic replanning, adaptive security policies, and context-aware isolation—are necessary to mitigate indirect prompt injection attacks on AI agents, shifting protection from model-only fixes to agent architecture and runtime controls.
problem_solved: Indirect prompt injection: malicious instructions embedded in untrusted data can coerce LLM-powered agents to take unsafe actions, and model-level mitigations alone are insufficient for dynamic, real-world tasks.
method: Dynamic replanning and security-policy updates: agents adapt plans at runtime while re-evaluating permissions and constraints when new input arrives.
Context-dependent isolation and capability restriction: isolate untrusted inputs, gate sensitive capabilities, and verify actions before execution (including human-in-the-loop or automated checks).
Monitoring, auditability, and fallback strategies: continuous observability, logging for post-hoc forensics, and safe fallback behaviors when policy verification fails.
impact: Provides a principled blueprint for architects of LLM-driven agents to reduce attack surface and operational risk by integrating policy, runtime checks, and verification—enabling safer deployment of autonomous systems in dynamic environments.
visual_elements: Agent architecture flow: diagram showing trusted vs untrusted data paths, policy gate, verifier, and capability sandbox.
Decision loop timeline: visual of dynamic replanning cycle (perception → policy check → plan → execute → audit) with intervention points highlighted.
Attack vs defense comparison: side-by-side examples of an indirect prompt injection exploit and how system-level defenses block or mitigate it.
Icon set: simple icons for 'isolation', 'policy update', 'human review', and 'audit log' to annotate workflows.
paper_title: Architecting Secure AI Agents: Perspectives on System-Level Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
paper_authors: Chong Xiang, Drew Zagieboylo, Shaona Ghosh, Sanjay Kariyappa, Kai Greshake
